ORIGINAL USMLE-STYLE PRACTICE

An adjunct in severe exacerbation

A patient with a severe asthma exacerbation receives repeated inhaled short-acting beta agonist treatment and systemic corticosteroids. Ipratropium is added during initial emergency care. Which description best captures its role in this setting?

  1. A substitute for all systemic corticosteroid treatment
  2. An antimicrobial treatment for all asthma attacks
  3. A leukotriene receptor antagonist taken orally
  4. A replacement for respiratory support when needed
  5. An additional bronchodilator acting through muscarinic blockade
Answer and explanation

An additional bronchodilator acting through muscarinic blockade

Ipratropium can add bronchodilation in severe acute asthma; it does not replace anti-inflammatory treatment.

Option explanations

An additional bronchodilator acting through muscarinic blockade: Ipratropium can add bronchodilation in severe acute asthma; it does not replace anti-inflammatory treatment.

A substitute for all systemic corticosteroid treatment: It does not replace the indicated anti-inflammatory therapy.

An antimicrobial treatment for all asthma attacks: It is not an antibiotic.

A leukotriene receptor antagonist taken orally: It is an inhaled antimuscarinic.

A replacement for respiratory support when needed: Medication does not replace necessary support in respiratory failure.
